correctness.rationale: For n≥1 and 0<β<1, a_n(x)=ln(1+βx/n)/ln(1+β/n) defines finite absorbing binomial chain on nodes j/n with endpoints absorbing; from any interior node one-step absorption has strictly positive probability, ensuring uniform geometric long-iteration limit. For Φγ(x)=(1−e^(−γx))/(1−e^(−γ)), exact binomial moment P_n e^(−γ·)=[1−a_n(1−e^(−γ/n))]^n yields super/subharmonicity equivalent to comparing a_n against normalized exponential F_{γ/n}. The logarithmic derivative ratio has derivative γ/n−(β/n)/(1+(β/n)x). At γ=β/(1+β/n) and β its signs force strict interior lower/upper Φ barriers; iteration preserves inequalities. ∂γΦγ is difference of conditional and unconditional means in [0,1], hence uniform error β²/(n+β). Multiplication by ln(1+μ+x) conjugates the original operator. n=1 endpoints, μ>0, x=0,1 and order-of-limits example are covered. Independent 15 node-system solutions and 75 interior inequalities corroborate but do not prove universality.
